beats.name: open
beats.caption: the problem: a finished render that lied
beats.vo: Agents can write a Blender render script. They cannot tell if the frames on disk are from this job, or the last one.

beats.name: stale
beats.caption: klieg jobs verify - stale artefact refused
beats.vo: Klieg is a DCC bridge for Hermes. Watch verify catch a stale job: exit code zero, artefacts empty, stale count one.

beats.name: probe
beats.caption: probe hosts | plan without running
beats.vo: Same session. Probe what is installed. Plan the pass without touching the GPU. Two hundred eighty eight frames, predicted duration from this machine's history.

beats.name: render
beats.caption: detached render | job dir survives the shell
beats.vo: Render detaches. The shell can die. The job keeps its own log, exit file, and status. When it finishes, verify does not trust the exit code alone.

beats.name: verify_ok
beats.caption: verify: mtime and count, not hope
beats.vo: Verify asks three questions. Does the file exist. Is its mtime newer than the job start. Did we get every frame we promised.

beats.name: result
beats.caption: result: frames on disk from this job
beats.vo: These are the frames that job wrote, read straight off disk. A count without a fresh mtime would still fail.

beats.name: board
beats.caption: how it works
beats.vo: Agent calls a verb. Approval gate. Adapter builds argv. One GPU lock. Job directory. Verify is the only claim that matters.

beats.name: end
beats.vo: Klieg. A DCC bridge for Hermes. The render that cannot lie about finishing. github.com slash LangerSword slash hermes-klieg.
